{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash

# Flux batch script (translated from PBS)

# PBS requested:
#   -N bead-select
#   -l procs=1,walltime=100:00:00,mem=7GB
#   -q WitsLong
#   -t 0-1024   (job array)

# This PBS script is a job array (0-1024). Flux has no single universally portable "job array" directive.
# Provide the array index via environment variable ARRAY_INDEX when submitting.
# Example: ARRAY_INDEX=0 flux batch <this_script>

flux alloc \
  -n 1 \
  --time=100h \
  --queue=WitsLong \
  bash -lc '

# NOTE: PBS mem=7GB has no universally portable Flux directive in a batch script.
# Performance implication: without a memory request/limit, the job may be placed where less memory is available,
# increasing risk of OOM or contention.

# NOTE: PBS job name (-N bead-select) has no universally portable Flux batch directive.
# Performance implication: none (metadata only), but job identification in monitoring/accounting may be less clear.

# NOTE: PBS array semantics (-t 0-1024 and $PBS_ARRAYID) have no universally portable Flux batch directive.
# Performance implication: you lose scheduler-managed array concurrency/throttling; submitting many jobs at once
# may affect throughput and queue behavior.

hostname

cd /spaces/scott/chip/pool_selection/

: "${ARRAY_INDEX:?ARRAY_INDEX must be set (0-1024) to replace PBS_ARRAYID}"
run=${ARRAY_INDEX}

/usr/bin/time python pool_select.py --input all.cpickle --label S${LABEL} --bad badscore60.lst \
  --requests extra.lst,req_func_u.scores --factor 1.5 $run 10 18
'
"
}
